title: grove backup: declare bucket name, grove name, and root aws reach on the box
description:
## .what

dev-env-setup#169 (the grove backup agent) is built against these declarations. each is owed from #63 / #64; the agent fails loud, by name, until each lands.

## .asks

1. **the bucket name on the box**: write `/etc/grove/backup.bucket` (one line, mode 644) from `CAMP_GROVE_BUCKET_NAME` itself, beside `/etc/grove/platform`. dev-env-setup is public, so the literal can never be typed there; this file is its one channel (dev-env-setup fulcrum F1, ruled A).
2. **the grove name on the box**: write `/etc/grove/name` (one line, the grove slug, mode 644). the backup key prefix is `grove=<slug>/`; a guessed name would let two groves overwrite each other.
3. **root's aws reach on hetzner**: #64 points camper's `[default]` at the roles-anywhere loopback helper; the agent runs as root via systemd. write `/etc/grove/aws.env` (systemd EnvironmentFile syntax, e.g. `AWS_EC2_METADATA_SERVICE_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`) so the unit reads the endpoint rather than a port typed in dev-env-setup. absent on ec2 = the instance profile answers.
4. **`GROVE_BACKUP_SCOPE` on main**: it sits on #64's branch; dev-env-setup clamps its dirs + excludes to it by test.
5. **the backup line in grove stats**: `git.grove.stats` and `hetzner.grove.probe` render one line from world-readable `/var/lib/grove-backup/status.json` (shape in the dev-env-setup#169 pr).
6. **a fresh grove of each kind** to prove the restore end to end.

## .if ask 1 is refused

say so on this issue. the fallback (a json the box reads from this repo) needs a grove credential that reads ahbode/infrastructure. that is a director call on the dev-env-setup side, so the drive halts there until it is made.
